newsitem.title: HONG KONG: KMB, Citybus to invest in airport fleets.
newsitem.headline: KMB, Citybus to invest in airport fleets.

text.p: Kowloon Motor Bus Co (1993) Ltd (KMB) and Citybus Ltd, a unit of CNT Group Ltd, will invest a total HK$300 million in buses serving routes to Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok.
Kowloon Motor Bus said in a statement that its wholly owned Long Win Holdings Ltd would pay HK$200 million for 125 buses.
Citybus said in a separate statement that it would buy 50 new double-deckers for HK$100 million.

Citybus' managing director Lyndon Rees said a further 60 new vehicles would be required for delivery by May 1998 for the airport bus and coach network. "Confirmation of this order will be placed in due course," Rees added.
Neither disclosed which companies would supply the vehicles.
The Hong Kong government approved the grant of new bus franchises to Citybus and Long Win to operate a total 25 public bus routes serving the new airport at Chek Lap Kok and North Lantau.
Citybus will run 13 routes and Long Win the other 12.
The government said the two bus franchises would run for six years from June 1, 1997, and no profit control scheme would be applied.
Seven routes will start operating in mid-1997 and the entire bus network will be in full operation upon the opening of the new airport in 1998, the government said.
